entities.summary:
Gao Ming, also known as Kao Ming, Gao Zecheng, and the Cabbage Root Taoist, was a Chinese poet and playwright during the Yuan Dynasty (1271–1368).

Born in a remote province in northern China, Gao Ming rose to prominence through his mastery of classical Chinese poetry and his innovative use of the cabbages as a metaphor for spiritual growth. His works, such as the 'Jade Mountain' and 'The Cabbage Root', were widely read and admired by the ruling Yuan Dynasty elite.

Gao Ming's influence extended beyond his own time, as his poetry and plays helped shape the cultural identity of the Mongol-influenced Yuan Dynasty. His legacy can be seen in the continued popularity of his works, which are still studied and performed today in China.

One of Gao Ming's most striking achievements was his ability to transcend the boundaries of his time, as his poetry and plays addressed universal themes of love, nature, and the human condition. His works continue to inspire new generations of artists, writers, and scholars.

Despite his enduring influence, Gao Ming's life was marked by controversy and criticism. His use of the cabbages as a metaphor for spiritual growth was seen as unusual and even subversive by some, leading to accusations of heresy and obscenity.

In recent years, Gao Ming's reputation has undergone a significant reevaluation, as scholars have sought to recontextualize his works within the broader cultural and historical landscape of the Yuan Dynasty. His legacy serves as a reminder of the complex and often fraught nature of cultural exchange and transmission in premodern China.
